title: Tenant Gatekeeper: observability proxy and incident playbook for Dedicated & On‑Prem
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers running VPC/on‑prem collectors have opaque failure modes when a single tenant produces a surge of bad telemetry (e.g., infinite sampling, malformed envelopes). This leads to downstream backpressure, noisy SLO alerts, and incident triage friction.

Goal: Ship a light-weight "Tenant Gatekeeper" observability proxy component and an associated incident playbook that: 1) enforces tenant-level ingestion budgets, 2) transparently quarantines malformed or high-cardinality payloads for offline analysis, 3) attaches stable tracing hooks and tenant-affinity headers so traces/metrics/logs can be correlated across relays/collectors, and 4) exposes tenant-scoped latency / error dashboards for on-call.

Non-goals: Not attempting to redesign the entire collector pipeline (no heavy protocol rewrites). Not replacing per-customer ingest SLAs or billing systems. This is a protective layer and operational playbook to reduce noisy-oncall churn.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper proxy can enforce per-tenant QPS and tokenized token-bucket on incoming traces/metrics/logs (configurable via customer profile)
Malformed or excessively large envelopes are quarantined to a customer-scoped quarantine S3/KV with an audit event emitted; normal path preserves <1% median added latency
Tracing hooks: proxy injects stable trace-context and tenant-affinity header (redwood-tenant-id) and preserves original span ids; verified on three representative ingestion clients
Dashboards: per-tenant latency and error-rate dashboards created (console link) with prebuilt alerts; dashboards show before/after baseline for pilot customers
Playbook: documented incident steps (quarantine playback, tenant throttling, rollbacks) validated in tabletop run with SRE and Solutions Eng
E2E tests: synthetic tenant flood test and malformed-envelope replay pass in staging with asserted SLA thresholds
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Aisha to capture design + rollout scope; initial impact analysis attached.
2025-02-15: Architecture spike completed — prototype proxy based on lightweight Envoy filter + Lua; added POC to repo: github.com/redwood/obs-gatekeeper/tree/poc-envoy.

2025-02-20: Design review with SRE and Privacy; decision: use signed tenant envelope header rather than RBAC in first iteration to avoid customer onboarding delay. Security requested threat model doc (link below).
2025-02-25: Implemented quarantine queue backed by internal objectstore (s3-compatible); added telemetry counters for quarantine_rate, pass_rate, avg_proxy_latency_ms.
2025-03-01: Integration tests flaked under high cardinality metrics — added heuristic cardinality-shedder and sampling policy. Open PR: github.com/redwood/obs-gatekeeper/pull/78.
2025-03-03: Tabletop incident run scheduled for 2025-03-10; Diego to lead playbook validation with pilot customer ACME Corp.
implementation_notes:
We chose an Envoy-based filter to minimize bootstrap time for onprem installs (customers already run Envoy in their perimeter). The filter will perform fast path validation and sampling decisions; heavy quarantine/enrichment is forwarded asynchronously to a background worker. Use of stable tenant header (signed by control plane) avoids deep authentication work in phase 1.

Trade-offs: Envoy filter keeps latency low but is harder to unit test than a standalone sidecar; we mitigate by extracting sampling logic into a small go library that is covered with unit tests and used by both filter and worker. Quarantine storage is eventually consistent; to keep replay integrity we include a monotonic ingest sequence attached to quarantined envelopes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated; deploy gatekeeper to staging for 2 pilot customers (ACME, NovaPay), 2) Run 48h flood + malformed replay tests, 3) Enable quarantine and alerts in canary region for pilot customers, 4) Run tabletop incident with SRE and Solutions Eng, 5) Gradual rollout to additional Dedicated clusters with opt-in, 6) GA with docs and SDK changes to expose tenant headers.
qa_plan: Automated e2e tests in CI: a) synthetic tenant flood at 5x expected peak, assert that other tenants' latency remains within SLO b) malformed-envelope injection asserts quarantine counters increment and alerts fire c) replay job can restore envelopes from quarantine and reprocess them to a dry-run path. Manual verification: runbook walkthrough and canary monitoring for 72h.
risks_mitigation: Risk: false positives in quarantine could hide valid customer telemetry -> Mitigation: expose quick restore button in console and track false_positive_rate metric
Risk: increased tail latency -> Mitigation: perf budget for proxy <= 3ms p50 and <= 20ms p99; heavy processing async
Risk: operator complexity on onprem installs -> Mitigation: provide a packaged helm chart and a diagnostic command to surface tenant quotas and last-quarantine samples
notes_for_reviewers: Please review the sampling heuristics in the design doc and the threat model before code review. Security review requested — see SSEC ticket #SSEC-314. The PR currently contains integration tests but needs mock envoy harness for CI; help from infra team (Kyle) appreciated.
